comparisons.title: Psoriasis Biologic Classes
comparisons.subtitle: Agent-specific indications and comorbid domains matter more than a single class ranking

values.tnf: Adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab, certolizumab pegol. (Golimumab treats PsA but does not have a plaque-psoriasis indication.)
values.il17: Secukinumab, ixekizumab, brodalumab, bimekizumab. PsA indications are agent-specific; brodalumab is plaque-psoriasis only.
values.il23: Guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab. PsA and IBD indications are agent-specific and continue to evolve.

values.tnf: Effective and broadly experienced; infliximab can act rapidly. Average complete-clearance rates are generally lower than with newer IL-17/IL-23 agents.
values.il17: Often the fastest high-level skin clearance; useful when rapid improvement or concurrent axial/peripheral PsA is a priority.
values.il23: High and durable skin clearance with relatively infrequent maintenance dosing; onset may be slower than the fastest IL-17 agents.
values.il1223: Durable established efficacy and convenient dosing, but average skin clearance is generally lower than newer IL-17/IL-23 agents.

values.tnf: Strong across peripheral arthritis, axial disease, enthesitis and dactylitis; extensive long-term evidence.
values.il17: Strong for peripheral and axial PsA, enthesitis and dactylitis; confirm the selected agent has the required indication.
values.il23: Effective for peripheral PsA, enthesitis and dactylitis for selected agents; not a preferred mechanism for clinically active axial disease.
values.il1223: Effective for peripheral PsA; not preferred for active axial disease.

values.tnf: Monoclonal TNF agents such as adalimumab, infliximab and certolizumab have IBD roles; etanercept does not treat IBD.
values.il17: Generally avoid in active IBD or choose only after gastroenterology discussion because new-onset/exacerbated IBD has been reported.
values.il23: Some agents have Crohn disease and/or ulcerative-colitis indications; select the exact agent for the bowel phenotype.
values.il1223: Ustekinumab treats Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis and can unify skin, joint and bowel treatment.

values.tnf: A monoclonal TNF inhibitor is generally preferred when recurrent uveitis is a major domain; etanercept is not preferred.
values.il17: May treat axial disease but is not the usual first choice for recurrent uveitis.
values.il23: Insufficient evidence to prioritize for uveitis.

values.tnf: Serious infection/TB and HBV reactivation; avoid or use cautiously with demyelinating disease and moderate–severe heart failure; paradoxical psoriasis and lupus-like reactions can occur.
values.il17: Mucocutaneous candidiasis and neutropenia can occur; IBD warning. Brodalumab has a boxed warning for suicidal ideation/behavior and a REMS program.
values.il23: Infection and hypersensitivity precautions; no basis for calling the class universally 'safest.' Long-term and patient-specific risks still matter.
values.il1223: Infection/TB precautions; rare serious hypersensitivity and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome have been reported.

values.tnf: Certolizumab has minimal placental transfer and the most supportive pregnancy pharmacokinetic data in this class; other TNF agents require trimester- and disease-specific planning.
values.il17: Human pregnancy data are more limited; use individualized maternal–fetal risk assessment.
values.il23: Human pregnancy data are more limited; use individualized maternal–fetal risk assessment.
values.il1223: Pregnancy registry/observational data exist but decisions remain individualized.

values.tnf: TB screen; HBV risk assessment; vaccines and infection review; agent/comorbidity-specific labs.
values.il17: TB/infection review; monitor candidiasis, IBD symptoms and neutropenia risk.
values.il23: TB/infection review and agent-specific laboratory/label monitoring.

features.name: When the class is often attractive

values.tnf: Need one mechanism for PsA plus IBD/uveitis, pregnancy planning with certolizumab, or extensive prior experience.
values.il17: Rapid skin clearance or strong axial/peripheral joint efficacy without active IBD.
values.il23: Durable high skin efficacy, convenient dosing, and selected peripheral PsA/IBD needs.
values.il1223: Established long-interval therapy, especially when IBD is also present and newer-class selection is not preferred.

citations.quote: AAD-NPF guideline reviews biologic treatment selection and monitoring in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
GRAPPA recommends domain-based PsA treatment that accounts for skin, joints, axial disease, enthesitis, dactylitis, associated conditions, and comorbidities.
EULAR 2023 PsA update links pharmacologic escalation to active domains, treatment targets, and extra-musculoskeletal manifestations.
Current SILIQ safety information describes the boxed warning for suicidal ideation/behavior and restricted distribution through the SILIQ REMS.
